narrative.overview:
Field Guide uses scientific field-guide classification to make work identifiable at a glance: task titles, compact labeled states and subordinate evidence. A generated personal palette frames work surfaces; restrained accents mark selection and action. Controls and text use system sans, with JetBrains Mono reserved for identifiers and logs.

Standard web controls and the plugin composition model remain intact. Panels share an index-like rhythm of identity, state and aligned evidence; tab selection and collapse occupy one header row. One generated personal theme applies throughout the app. Hue, saturation, brightness, appearance and color harmony derive the palette; previous preset and saved palettes are discarded. Motion provides bounded state feedback with reduced-motion support.
keyCharacteristics: Theme-derived navigation and work surfaces with restrained selection accents.
Task identity first, labeled state alongside it, supporting evidence below.
System sans for controls and text; JetBrains Mono for identifiers and logs.
Twelve-pixel panels and six-pixel controls, with native affordances.
Customizable panels, logs within reach and a single-column small-screen reading order.

Across 16 generic composition pages and both Helm implementations, compact header Refresh and Edit icon buttons leave stacked tabs usable. Edit becomes Done and reveals the named Page customization region with Add, Hide/Show and Remove controls; removal saves the layout and disposes only the removed panel without stopping underlying work.

rules.name: The Generated Theme Rule
rules.body: Use semantic CSS properties for surfaces, text, selection and state. A single browser-local recipe generates the personal palette in OKLCH, with gamut-mapped sRGB output. Analogous harmony offsets the companion hue by 35°; complementary uses 180°; triadic uses 120° for the companion and 240° for lightly tinted surfaces. Tetradic distributes four hues at 0°, 60°, 180° and 240°; Square uses 0°, 90°, 180° and 270°. Split complementary uses 0°, 150° and 210°. Monochromatic varies lightness and chroma at one hue; Shades darkens the companion at the base hue while retaining its chroma before gamut mapping. Available user-supplied five-color presets are Ember Tide, Olive & Copper, Festival, Spring Tide and Daydream. Five-color palettes assign seeds to background, text, accents and panels by lightness and chroma; Palette colors preserves original hue relationships, while another harmony deliberately changes them. Source colors remain stored in the recipe and explicit overrides apply last. Error, success, review and queued stay in their red, green, blue and yellow families. Previous presets and saved palettes are removed; only the current generated theme is saved.

rules.name: The Custom Contrast Rule
rules.body: Generated palettes and advanced overrides preserve raw fills. Derive shared text foregrounds toward 4.5:1 contrast on the background, navigation and panels when those surfaces permit a shared foreground. Derive input values and placeholders independently to at least 4.5:1 against the selected Input background; changing that ground does not change page text. Native range controls derive input-accent against that ground; shared keyboard-focus outlines use accent-text. Filled-action ink follows the actual fill brightness independently of theme mode. A shared foreground cannot guarantee contrast across arbitrary mixed light and dark surfaces.

rules.name: The Identity First Rule
rules.body: Give the task title priority, keep identifiers and evidence subordinate, and write the state as a label rather than relying on color alone.

rules.name: The Named Panel Rule
rules.body: Within a named panel tab, visually hide a repeated local heading while keeping it available to assistive technology. Preserve the heading when the plugin is rendered standalone.

rules.name: The Flat Work Surface Rule
rules.body: Separate work panels with neutral surface tone, spacing and thin borders. Reserve floating depth for the notification popover.

rules.name: The Color Wheel Rule
rules.body: A code-rendered OKLCH color wheel chooses hue by angle (0° right, 90° top, 180° left, 270° bottom) and brightness by radius (white center to black rim); Saturation adjusts its coloration. A white-and-black selection ring stays visible across the wheel; its keyboard-focus outline uses the derived neutral text color outside the rainbow field. Mouse and touch drags capture the pointer and clamp at the rim; cancel, removal and destruction release it. The focusable labeled wheel accepts Left/Right for hue and Up/Down for brightness, with Shift for ten-unit steps; native sliders provide precise accessible alternatives. The wheel and sliders update together without replacing controls, and preserve palette sources and advanced overrides. Desktop places the wheel beside the sliders; small screens stack them. Canvas painting coalesces saturation/resize changes, caps its internal raster at 256 pixels, and uses the same gamut mapper as theme generation; hue/brightness updates move the marker without repainting.

rules.name: The Launch Icon Rule
rules.body: New Run places an (18px) Phosphor Fill icon before its launch label with an (8px) gap: anchor for Weigh anchor in Pirate mode, play for Start run otherwise. Icons inherit the button foreground and remain hidden from assistive technology; the label and focus identity remain stable.

rules.name: The Integration Status Rule
rules.body: Jira and GitHub links in Config include (16px) status icons in the navigation foreground. Distinct check, warning, slash, question and clock shapes identify verified, unavailable, not configured, unknown and checking states; hover text and accessible descriptions explain each result while preserving the link name. Jira verifies account authentication; GitHub also verifies pull request access for the header galleon when selected. Checks refresh on Config navigation, scope changes, explicit refresh and successful credential updates, with a bounded cache and no background polling.

rules.name: The Plain Selection and PR Results Rule
rules.body: Campaign panels use “Use top selection” to restore the galleon selection made at the top of Helmsman. The PR page inherits that selection without a permanent reset control. Inspection leads the page, with selected detail and diff immediately below it. Close inspection appears for a selected PR and remains available if closing fails, so restoring the top selection can be retried without changing it. The composed page owns one Refresh action; a standalone PR panel retains its own. PR lists use independent-height desktop columns and document flow on mobile, without inner list scrollbars. Full-width title-first selection controls lead each row; PR number, state, date and known meaningful counts are subordinate. Compact notices distinguish confirmed empty lists from incomplete reads, retain readable results, and offer a scoped full-list action. Recent PR runs sit after the lists in a collapsed native disclosure that preserves its open state during refresh.

rules.name: The Bounties Contrast Rule
rules.body: PR inspection uses the stronger panel-hi ground and an accent-filled Load action, with paired accent ink. Lists retain neutral panel ground; recent history recedes to canvas ground. Local Phosphor Regular icons identify sections, review actions and labeled states. Red marks failures and requested changes, green marks success, blue marks review, and yellow marks pending checks. Status labels stay readable independently of color; icons and their license ship with the standalone plugin.

rules.name: The Triage Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Triage has one composed Refresh and page heading, with a standalone fallback. A contrasting panel-2 filter band groups labeled source, priority, update window and page-size controls. Backlog, To do and My open work columns use panel-hi headers over panel ground; source context is subordinate and the header galleon is not repeated. Same-label sources retain distinguishing instance identifiers. Task titles use readable body ink, with ticket identifiers, readable UTC dates, labeled states and priority flags below. Local Phosphor icons identify task states, priority and launch. Description toggles and contextual assignment, launch and related-run actions stay compact; columns flow vertically on small screens, with 44px coarse-pointer controls. Saved selection, filters, descriptions, collapse state, paging and command recovery remain intact; unsupported saved selection still permits choosing a source.

rules.name: The Global Terminal Rule
rules.body: Terminal is a global view of the connected terminal app, explicitly independent of galleon scope. It selects All through the public panel scope service before reads, including for old saved scoped panels, and fails closed with Refresh guidance if scope restoration fails. The header galleon selector is hidden on Terminal routes while its selection stays mounted and returns unchanged on other pages. The composed page owns the single heading and Refresh; standalone panels retain their own. A contrasting connection band and compact tab rail lead into the dominant plaintext screen preview. Connected with no open tabs and unavailable connection have distinct compact empty states. Phosphor icons accompany connection and control labels; fonts and licenses ship inside the plugin. Polling preserves screen scroll, input focus and per-target drafts. Keyboard capture remains explicit, and every control and saved receipt retains its original target and request identity. Tab previews show the latest user prompt when the native provider can bind it to the active agent transcript, with a three-line plain-text preview and full supplied text in a tooltip. Unsupported or unreadable prompts use an explicit unavailable state. Prompt changes preserve the focused tab button and never alter control identities.

dos: Do use semantic theme properties so generated colors and advanced overrides apply consistently.
Do present task titles, labeled states and subordinate evidence in the shared index-like rhythm.
Do preserve the accessible heading when suppressing a repeated visible panel heading.
Do keep tab selection and collapse together, and preserve saved panel order when adapting to a narrow screen.
Do use visible focus outlines and honor reduced-motion preferences.
Do provide coarse-pointer targets of at least (44px) without increasing fine-pointer-only density.
Do preserve keyboard focus through redraws and expose loading with readable status text.
donts: Don't restore brushed-metal panels, seven-segment counts or the oscilloscope treatment as the default visual language.
Don't use monospace as the general control or prose face.
Don't use a status hue as the only way to identify state.
Don't turn a viewport change into a saved layout edit.
